USA.name: Contiguous U.S.
USA.description: The 48 contiguous states plus D.C. — the U.S. mainland.

USA.name: Alaska
USA.description: The largest U.S. state by area — bought from Russia in 1867 for $7.2 million.

USA.name: Hawaii
USA.description: A volcanic archipelago in the Central Pacific; the 50th state, admitted in 1959.

USA.name: Puerto Rico
USA.description: The most populous U.S. territory (~3.2M). Residents are U.S. citizens but cannot vote in presidential elections.

USA.name: U.S. Virgin Islands
USA.description: A Caribbean territory bought from Denmark in 1917 — St. Thomas, St. John, and St. Croix.

USA.name: Guam
USA.description: A strategic island in Micronesia hosting major U.S. military bases.

USA.name: American Samoa
USA.description: The southernmost U.S. territory; people born here are U.S. nationals, not citizens by birth.

USA.name: Northern Mariana Islands
USA.description: A commonwealth in the Western Pacific, centered on the island of Saipan.

USA.name: U.S. Minor Outlying Islands
USA.description: Nine small, mostly uninhabited islands across the Pacific and Caribbean: Baker, Howland, Jarvis, Johnston, Kingman, Midway, Palmyra, Wake, and Navassa.

FRA.name: Metropolitan France
FRA.description: European France — the mainland often called l’Hexagone.

FRA.name: French Guiana
FRA.badge: Overseas department and region of France
FRA.description: On the northeast coast of South America — home to the Guiana Space Centre, the EU’s spaceport.

FRA.name: Guadeloupe
FRA.badge: Overseas department and region of France
FRA.description: A Caribbean archipelago shaped like a butterfly; an integral part of France and the EU.

FRA.name: Martinique
FRA.badge: Overseas department and region of France
FRA.description: A volcanic Caribbean island dominated by Mont Pelée.

FRA.name: Réunion
FRA.badge: Overseas department and region of France
FRA.description: An island in the Indian Ocean east of Madagascar; the EU’s outermost region in that ocean.

FRA.name: Mayotte
FRA.badge: Overseas department and region of France
FRA.description: An island in the Mozambique Channel; France’s newest overseas department (2011).

FRA.name: French Polynesia
FRA.description: An autonomous collectivity of 118 islands across the South Pacific, including Tahiti.

FRA.name: New Caledonia
FRA.description: A South Pacific archipelago with a unique self-governing status and a path toward possible independence.

FRA.name: St. Pierre & Miquelon
FRA.description: A small archipelago off Newfoundland — the last remnant of New France in North America.

FRA.name: Wallis & Futuna
FRA.description: A Polynesian collectivity in the South Pacific governed alongside three traditional kingdoms.

FRA.name: Saint-Barthélemy
FRA.description: A small, affluent Caribbean island that left Guadeloupe to become its own collectivity in 2007.

FRA.name: Saint-Martin
FRA.description: The French northern half of the island of Saint Martin, shared with Dutch Sint Maarten.

FRA.name: French Southern & Antarctic Lands
FRA.description: Scattered sub-Antarctic islands (Kerguelen, Crozet…) plus a claimed slice of Antarctica — only research staff live there.

FRA.name: Clipperton Island
FRA.badge: Overseas state private property of France
FRA.description: An uninhabited coral atoll in the eastern Pacific — France’s only atoll.

NLD.name: European Netherlands
NLD.description: The European part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

NLD.name: Caribbean Netherlands
NLD.description: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, and Saba — three Caribbean islands that are part of the Netherlands proper.

NLD.name: Aruba
NLD.badge: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands
NLD.description: A self-governing country of the Kingdom off the coast of Venezuela.

NLD.name: Curaçao
NLD.badge: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands
NLD.description: The largest of the Dutch Caribbean countries, with a strong autonomy.

NLD.name: Sint Maarten
NLD.badge: Constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands
NLD.description: The Dutch southern half of Saint Martin, shared with French Saint-Martin.

NOR.name: Mainland Norway
NOR.description: Mainland Norway on the Scandinavian Peninsula.

NOR.name: Svalbard
NOR.description: A high-Arctic archipelago governed by the 1920 Svalbard Treaty, open to all signatory nations for commerce.

NOR.name: Jan Mayen
NOR.description: A remote volcanic island in the Arctic Ocean, home only to military and meteorological staff.

NOR.name: Bouvet Island
NOR.description: A glacier-covered sub-Antarctic island — one of the most remote places on Earth.

ECU.name: Mainland Ecuador
ECU.description: Continental Ecuador on the Pacific coast of South America.

ECU.name: Galápagos Islands
ECU.description: A volcanic archipelago ~1,000 km off the mainland whose wildlife inspired Darwin’s theory of evolution.

GBR.name: Great Britain
GBR.description: Great Britain and Northern Ireland — the United Kingdom’s home nations.

GBR.name: Gibraltar
GBR.description: A strategic rocky headland at the entrance to the Mediterranean, held by Britain since 1713.

GBR.name: Bermuda
GBR.description: An affluent North Atlantic island group ~1,000 km off the U.S. east coast.

GBR.name: Cayman Islands
GBR.description: A Caribbean territory and major offshore financial centre.

GBR.name: British Virgin Islands
GBR.description: A Caribbean archipelago east of Puerto Rico, a popular sailing destination.

GBR.name: Turks & Caicos
GBR.description: A low-lying Caribbean archipelago southeast of the Bahamas.

GBR.name: Anguilla
GBR.description: A small flat Caribbean island in the northern Leeward Islands.

GBR.name: Montserrat
GBR.description: A Caribbean island half-buried by the still-active Soufrière Hills volcano.

GBR.name: Falkland Islands
GBR.description: A South Atlantic archipelago east of Argentina, the focus of the 1982 war.

GBR.name: St Helena, Ascension & Tristan da Cunha
GBR.description: Three remote South Atlantic island groups — Napoleon’s final exile was on St Helena.

GBR.name: Pitcairn Islands
GBR.description: A tiny South Pacific group settled by the Bounty mutineers; ~40 inhabitants.

GBR.name: Isle of Man
GBR.description: A self-governing island in the Irish Sea with its own ancient parliament, Tynwald.

GBR.name: Jersey
GBR.description: The largest Channel Island, off the coast of Normandy.

GBR.name: Guernsey
GBR.description: A Channel Island bailiwick off the coast of Normandy.

GBR.name: British Indian Ocean Territory
GBR.description: The Chagos Archipelago, hosting the joint UK–US base on Diego Garcia.

GBR.name: South Georgia & South Sandwich Is.
GBR.description: Sub-Antarctic islands with no permanent population, only research and support staff.

GBR.name: Akrotiri
GBR.description: A British military base area on Cyprus retained at independence in 1960.

GBR.name: Dhekelia
GBR.description: A British military base area on Cyprus retained at independence in 1960.

AUS.name: Norfolk Island
AUS.description: A small South Pacific island once used as a penal colony, settled partly by Bounty descendants.

AUS.name: Christmas & Cocos (Keeling) Islands
AUS.description: Australia’s Indian Ocean territories — Christmas Island’s red-crab migration is world-famous.

AUS.name: Coral Sea Islands
AUS.description: Scattered uninhabited reefs and cays northeast of Queensland.

AUS.name: Heard & McDonald Islands
AUS.description: Subantarctic volcanic islands with Australia’s only active volcano; no permanent residents.

AUS.name: Ashmore & Cartier Islands
AUS.description: Uninhabited Indian Ocean islets off the northwest coast.

DNK.name: Greenland
DNK.badge: Autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark
DNK.description: The world’s largest island, self-governing since 2009, mostly covered by ice sheet.

DNK.name: Faroe Islands
DNK.badge: Autonomous territory of the Kingdom of Denmark
DNK.description: A self-governing North Atlantic archipelago between Scotland and Iceland.

CHN.name: Hong Kong
CHN.description: A former British colony returned in 1997; a global financial hub with its own legal system.

CHN.name: Macau
CHN.description: A former Portuguese colony returned in 1999, now the world’s largest gambling centre.

NZL.name: Mainland New Zealand
NZL.description: The North and South Islands of New Zealand.

NZL.name: Chatham Islands
NZL.description: A small archipelago ~800 km east of the South Island, the first inhabited land to see each new day.

NZL.name: Cook Islands
NZL.description: A self-governing South Pacific nation in free association with New Zealand.

NZL.name: Niue
NZL.description: One of the world’s largest raised coral atolls, self-governing in association with New Zealand.

ESP.name: Mainland Spain
ESP.description: Peninsular Spain on the Iberian Peninsula.

ESP.name: Canary Islands
ESP.description: A volcanic archipelago off northwest Africa — an outermost region of the EU.

PRT.name: Mainland Portugal
PRT.description: Mainland Portugal on the Iberian Peninsula.

PRT.name: Azores
PRT.description: A mid-Atlantic volcanic archipelago, the westernmost point of Europe.

PRT.name: Madeira
PRT.description: A subtropical Atlantic island famed for its fortified wine and steep terrain.

CHL.name: Mainland Chile
CHL.description: Continental Chile along South America’s Pacific coast.

CHL.name: Easter Island
CHL.description: Rapa Nui — one of the most remote inhabited islands on Earth, famed for its moai statues.

FIN.name: Åland Islands
FIN.description: A Swedish-speaking, demilitarised archipelago between Finland and Sweden.
